label: Langtang yak cheese
note: Swiss-style cheese made at Kyangjin since the 1950s; taught by Swiss cheesemakers (Werner Schulthess, Sepp Dubach), Swiss project handed to the government in 1964

about.text: A hard cheese of the Langtang valley in Nepal, made from yak and nak (female yak) milk by the Swiss method that Swiss cheesemakers brought to Kyangjin in the 1950s.

links.name: Nepali Times, The story of Langtang cheese

how.text: Output at Langtang: about 14 t of cheese and 2,000 kg of butter a year from about 63 farmers (Nepali Times). The sources compare it to Swiss cheese but name no Alpine type.

links.name: Nepali Times: The story of Langtang cheese

steps.note: In a large vat, or in cans in a hot-water bath over a wood fire to about 71 °C at Chandanbari (Cheese Professor).
With a cheese culture or rennet, species not named in any source.

steps.name: cut and stir
steps.note: Curd cut and stirred for 1.5 h, with and without fire.

steps.name: brine
steps.note: In salt water so the rind is salty.
